title: Source-verified literature and bounded novelty positioning

query_families: exact INX Future Inc name and acquisition filename
employee performance prediction and machine learning
HR analytics with XAI or SHAP
leakage-aware model evaluation and nested cross-validation
explanation robustness, sensitivity, faithfulness, and SHAP stability
model reporting and reproducible machine-learning workflows
preferred_authorities: official PMLR, JMLR, or NeurIPS proceedings
authoritative open repository when no publisher record exists
search_protocol.selection_rule: Include 15 to 25 works that are directly empirical, use the same or a closely analogous HR dataset, or supply a method/governance requirement used by the shared evidence contract. Do not pad with generic AI papers.
search_protocol.doi_rule: A DOI is registered only when Crossref returned the work on the retrieval date. Publisher-asserted but unresolved identifiers remain explicitly qualified and must not be described as registry-verified.
search_protocol.access_rule: Assess methods from publisher full text when accessible; otherwise use the publisher abstract/metadata and mark unobserved design fields not_reported rather than infer their absence.

positioning_field_definitions.employee_performance: The modeled or substantively studied outcome is individual employee job performance; attrition-only work is not counted as employee performance.
positioning_field_definitions.same_or_similar_dataset: The work uses the exact 1,200-row INX dataset, exact HRDataset_v14, or another employee-level HR prediction dataset close enough to inform design comparison.
positioning_field_definitions.leakage_policy: An explicit prediction-time feature-availability or leakage-exclusion policy is stated beyond merely removing the target column.
positioning_field_definitions.nested_cv: All data-dependent model or hyperparameter selection is nested inside training partitions used for performance estimation.
positioning_field_definitions.calibration: Predicted probabilities are explicitly calibrated or evaluated as calibrated; reporting log loss alone does not qualify.
positioning_field_definitions.exact_fold_explanations: Each held-out explanation is generated by the exact model fitted without that held-out observation and model/fold identity is retained.
positioning_field_definitions.shap_stability: SHAP stability is quantitatively evaluated under repeated seeds, samples, resamples, folds, or controlled input perturbations; a single SHAP plot does not qualify.
positioning_field_definitions.subgroup_analysis: Predictive performance or errors are compared across supported demographic or organizational groups; discussion of fairness alone does not qualify.
positioning_field_definitions.proxy_reconstruction: The ability to reconstruct a protected or organizational attribute from retained predictors is explicitly tested.
positioning_field_definitions.second_dataset: The empirical method is evaluated on a genuinely distinct dataset, not only multiple tables from one organization or multiple train/test splits.
positioning_field_definitions.artifact_provenance: Machine-verifiable lineage binds reported outputs to source data, code/model/fold identity, environment, and immutable hashes; a data or code URL alone is insufficient.

novelty_boundary.bounded_claim: Within this 25-work, source-verified positioning set, no selected work reports the complete shared evidence contract used here.
novelty_boundary.mechanism: The contribution is a shared, hash-bound evidence contract connecting prediction-time feature policy, nested selection, exact held-out prediction and explanation identity, training-only calibration, explanation stability and faithfulness, subgroup/proxy claim boundaries, independent replication, and manuscript-number provenance.
prevented_failures: confounding feature-policy effects with hyperparameter retuning
unsupported fairness or discrimination inference from descriptive subgroup gaps
conflating protected-attribute reconstructability with actual proxy use by the performance model
untraceable or stale numerical claims in manuscript text

studies.authors: Archana B.; Sharma S.; Singh S.; Rafsan A.
studies.title: Application of Machine Learning in Employee Performance Prediction
studies.venue: International Journal of Computer Sciences and Engineering, 7(Special Issue 14), 443-447
studies.verification_basis: Publisher article record and publisher PDF identify the title, authors, 2019 issue, pages, INX source, and asserted DOI; Crossref returned 404 on 2026-09-07, so the DOI is not treated as registered.
studies.evidence_anchor: Publisher PDF abstract and dataset/method description.
studies.assessment_note: Direct same-dataset prior art comparing standard classifiers. No prediction-time availability contract, nested selection, probability calibration, SHAP audit, proxy audit, or immutable artifact lineage is reported in the accessible source.

studies.authors: Lather, Anu Singh; Malhotra, Ruchika; Saloni, Priya; Singh, Prabhjot; Mittal, Sarthak
studies.title: Prediction of Employee Performance Using Machine Learning Techniques
studies.venue: Proceedings of the 1st International Conference on Advanced Information Science and System, Article 30, 1-6
studies.verification_basis: Crossref and DBLP agree on title, authors, venue, year, and DOI; method details are limited to accessible bibliographic/secondary descriptions.
studies.evidence_anchor: Registered metadata plus the method summary cited in the RanKer related-work section.
studies.assessment_note: Employee-performance study using a self-created psychometric dataset and ordinary 10-fold validation; no evidence of nested tuning or the other audit controls was available.

studies.authors: Li, Merry Grace T.; Lazo, Macrina; Balan, Ariel Kelly; de Goma, Joel
studies.title: Employee Performance Prediction Using Different Supervised Classifiers
studies.venue: Proceedings of the 11th Annual International Conference on Industrial Engineering and Operations Management, 6870-6876
studies.verification_basis: Official IEOM proceedings index and full paper verify title, authors, venue, dates, pages, and method.
studies.evidence_anchor: Full paper Sections 3.2-3.5 and Results: three linked internal HR tables, feature list, models, validation metrics, and permutation importance.
studies.assessment_note: A related organization-specific employee-performance study with three joined source tables. It reports a validation result and permutation importance but no feature-timing policy, nested CV, calibration, protected-group audit, or reproducible artifact lineage.

studies.authors: Patel, Keyur; Sheth, Karan; Mehta, Dev; Tanwar, Sudeep; Florea, Bogdan Cristian; Taralunga, Dragos Daniel; Altameem, Ahmed; Altameem, Torki; Sharma, Ravi
studies.title: RanKer: An AI-Based Employee-Performance Classification Scheme to Rank and Identify Low Performers
studies.verification_basis: Crossref and MDPI records verify metadata and DOI; publisher full text verifies the exact 1,200-row, 28-field INX dataset and evaluation design.
studies.evidence_anchor: Full paper Sections 4.1 and 4.6-4.7: 80/20 split, separate validation curve, log loss, and public dataset link.
studies.assessment_note: Closest registered same-INX prior art. Cross-validation is a reported validation curve rather than nested selection; log loss is reported without calibration; no SHAP, subgroup/proxy, or hash-bound lineage audit is present.

studies.authors: Adeniyi, Jide Kehinde; Adeniyi, Abidemi Emmanuel; Oguns, Yetunde Josephine; Egbedokun, Gabriel Olumide; Ajagbe, Kehinde Douglas; Obuzor, Princewill Chima; Ajagbe, Sunday Adeola
studies.title: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Techniques for the Prediction of Employee Performance
studies.verification_basis: Publisher full text and Crossref verify metadata; the full text identifies Kaggle HRDataset_v14 through its 311-by-36 schema and cited source.
studies.evidence_anchor: Full text Dataset, Data Preprocessing, and Results sections: target, stated dropped columns, PCA, and one 80/20 split.
studies.assessment_note: Exact HRDataset_v14 comparator. The stated exclusion list does not document removal of PerfScoreID, a target-alias risk, and PCA is not described as training-only. The comparison uses one 80/20 split and does not audit calibration, explanations, subgroups, proxies, or artifact lineage.

studies.authors: Nayem, Zannatul; Uddin, Md. Aftab
studies.title: Unbiased Employee Performance Evaluation Using Machine Learning
studies.venue: Journal of Open Innovation: Technology, Market, and Complexity, 10(1), 100243
studies.verification_basis: Crossref and Elsevier publisher record verify metadata; publisher abstract verifies a newly collected 1,109-employee dataset and classifier comparison.
studies.evidence_anchor: Publisher abstract; design fields not visible there are marked not_reported.
studies.assessment_note: The title and abstract use unbiased/bias-free language, but the accessible publisher record does not establish the subgroup-performance, proxy, or evidence-lineage tests required for a fairness conclusion.

studies.authors: Abu-Faty, Hagar G.; Kafafy, Ahmed; Hadhoud, Mohiy M.; Abdel-Raouf, Osama
studies.title: Integrating Generative AI and Machine Learning Classifiers for Solving Heterogenous MCGDM: A Case of Employee Churn Prediction
studies.verification_basis: Crossref, Nature full text, and PMC verify metadata and methods; the INX dataset is explicitly the second dataset.
studies.evidence_anchor: Full text Results based on another dataset and ML evaluation sections: 80/20 split, 10-fold CV, two datasets, and data links.
studies.assessment_note: Uses exact INX as a second dataset in a churn/ranking framework and reports data URLs, but not prediction-time leakage policies, nested selection, calibration, exact-model explanations, proxy diagnostics, or immutable artifact hashes.

studies.authors: Putri, Jelly Helia; Sitohang, Sunarsan
studies.title: Klasifikasi Kinerja Pegawai Menggunakan Algoritma Random Forest
studies.verification_basis: Crossref and publisher full text verify metadata, exact INX dataset, and design.
studies.evidence_anchor: Full text Methods and Results: five train/test proportions, selection of the best test-split result, impurity feature importance, and stated limitations.
studies.assessment_note: Direct same-INX prior art. The reported best accuracy is chosen across multiple train/test proportions, which is not an isolated nested selection procedure. Feature importance is single-fit and non-SHAP; no calibration, subgroup/proxy, or provenance audit is reported.

studies.authors: Chaudhary, Meenu; Gaur, Loveleen; Chakrabarti, Amlan; Singh, Gurmeet; Jones, Paul; Kraus, Sascha
studies.title: An Integrated Model to Evaluate the Transparency in Predicting Employee Churn Using Explainable Artificial Intelligence
studies.verification_basis: Crossref and Elsevier publisher record verify metadata; publisher abstract verifies comparison of logistic regression and random forest with SHAP.
studies.evidence_anchor: Publisher abstract; unavailable lineage details are marked not_reported.
studies.assessment_note: Close HR-XAI comparator for employee churn. It applies SHAP to selected models, but the accessible source does not bind held-out explanations to exact fold models or quantify explanation stability.

studies.authors: Tambe, Prasanna; Cappelli, Peter; Yakubovich, Valery
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence in Human Resources Management: Challenges and a Path Forward
studies.verification_basis: Crossref and SAGE publisher record verify metadata and HR-AI scope.
studies.evidence_anchor: Publisher article framing of data limitations, fairness, employee reaction, and managerial constraints.
studies.assessment_note: Domain-governance source, not an empirical benchmark. It supports limiting technical claims to the practical and institutional constraints of HR decisions.

studies.authors: Leicht-Deobald, Ulrich; Busch, Thorsten; Schank, Christoph; Weibel, Antoinette; Schafheitle, Simon; Wildhaber, Isabelle; Kasper, Gabriel
studies.title: The Challenges of Algorithm-Based HR Decision-Making for Personal Integrity
studies.verification_basis: Crossref and Springer publisher record verify metadata and scope.
studies.evidence_anchor: Publisher article on personal integrity risks in algorithm-based HR decision-making.
studies.assessment_note: Normative HR source. It supports treating a model as decision support and avoiding automated prescriptive employee actions.

studies.authors: Köchling, Alina; Wehner, Marius Claus
studies.title: Discriminated by an Algorithm: A Systematic Review of Discrimination and Fairness by Algorithmic Decision-Making in the Context of HR Recruitment and HR Development
studies.verification_basis: Crossref and Springer full text verify metadata and the systematic review of 36 HR recruitment/development articles.
studies.evidence_anchor: Publisher abstract and systematic-review methods/results.
studies.assessment_note: Systematic governance review, not a predictive benchmark. It supports the distinction between descriptive subgroup diagnostics and demonstrated discrimination/fairness.

studies.authors: Giermindl, Lisa Marie; Strich, Franz; Christ, Oliver; Leicht-Deobald, Ulrich; Redzepi, Abdullah
studies.title: The Dark Sides of People Analytics: Reviewing the Perils for Organisations and Employees
studies.verification_basis: Crossref and Taylor & Francis publisher record verify metadata and scope.
studies.evidence_anchor: Publisher review of organizational and employee risks from people analytics.
studies.assessment_note: People-analytics risk review. It grounds the non-deployment, non-causal, and employee-impact boundaries of the technical evidence.

studies.authors: Lundberg, Scott M.; Lee, Su-In
studies.title: A Unified Approach to Interpreting Model Predictions
studies.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 30
studies.verification_basis: Official NeurIPS proceedings verify title, authors, venue, year, abstract, paper, reviews, and supplemental material.
studies.evidence_anchor: Official abstract and paper defining SHAP as an additive feature-attribution framework.
studies.assessment_note: Foundational SHAP method. It defines attribution semantics but does not by itself ensure causal interpretation, exact cross-validation model identity, or stability under model/data perturbation.

studies.authors: Lundberg, Scott M.; Erion, Gabriel; Chen, Hugh; DeGrave, Alex; Prutkin, Jordan M.; Nair, Bala; Katz, Ronit; Himmelfarb, Jonathan; Bansal, Nisha; Lee, Su-In
studies.title: From Local Explanations to Global Understanding with Explainable AI for Trees
studies.verification_basis: Crossref and Nature publisher metadata verify title, authors, venue, year, pages, and DOI.
studies.evidence_anchor: Publisher paper on exact tree SHAP computation and global aggregation of local explanations.
studies.assessment_note: Tree-SHAP foundation for exact model-output attribution. Exact SHAP computation is distinct from retaining the exact fold/model identity or demonstrating ranking stability.

studies.authors: Alvarez-Melis, David; Jaakkola, Tommi S.
studies.title: On the Robustness of Interpretability Methods
studies.verification_basis: The arXiv record and full text verify title, authors, date, method, and experiments.
studies.evidence_anchor: Full text Sections 2-3: local Lipschitz robustness and empirical SHAP/LIME explanation variation under nearby inputs.
studies.assessment_note: Direct explanation-robustness precedent that includes SHAP. It studies local input perturbations, not stability across model seeds, folds, or resampled training sets.

studies.authors: Yeh, Chih-Kuan; Hsieh, Cheng-Yu; Suggala, Arun; Inouye, David I.; Ravikumar, Pradeep
studies.title: On the (In)fidelity and Sensitivity of Explanations
studies.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 32
studies.verification_basis: Official NeurIPS proceedings verify title, authors, venue, year, abstract, full paper, reviews, and supplemental material.
studies.evidence_anchor: Official paper defining quantitative explanation infidelity and sensitivity under perturbations.
studies.assessment_note: Provides general objective explanation sensitivity/faithfulness measures. It motivates perturbation testing but is not a repeated SHAP rank-stability study.

studies.authors: Slack, Dylan; Hilgard, Sophie; Jia, Emily; Singh, Sameer; Lakkaraju, Himabindu
studies.title: Fooling LIME and SHAP: Adversarial Attacks on Post Hoc Explanation Methods
studies.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society, 180-186
studies.verification_basis: Crossref and ACM publisher metadata verify title, authors, venue, pages, year, and DOI.
studies.evidence_anchor: Publisher paper demonstrating that post-hoc perturbation explainers can be manipulated to conceal biased model behavior.
studies.assessment_note: Shows that plausible-looking SHAP outputs are not sufficient audit evidence. It addresses adversarial concealment rather than seed/resample stability or exact-fold lineage.

studies.authors: Cawley, Gavin C.; Talbot, Nicola L. C.
studies.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
studies.verification_basis: Official JMLR article record and full paper verify metadata, pages, and model-selection analysis.
studies.evidence_anchor: Full paper on overfitting the selection criterion and nested separation of selection from evaluation.
studies.assessment_note: Methodological basis for nested evaluation and for separating fixed-policy comparisons from independently retuned estimands.

studies.authors: Kaufman, Shachar; Rosset, Saharon; Perlich, Claudia; Stitelman, Ori
studies.title: Leakage in Data Mining: Formulation, Detection, and Avoidance
studies.venue: ACM Transactions on Knowledge Discovery from Data, 6(4), Article 15, 1-21
studies.verification_basis: Crossref and ACM publisher metadata verify title, authors, venue, article, pages, year, and DOI.
studies.evidence_anchor: Publisher paper formalizing leakage, its detection, and avoidance.
studies.assessment_note: Foundational leakage source. Its feature/label relationship analysis motivates explicit timing and target-proxy controls, though the present proxy-reconstruction estimand is more specific.

studies.authors: Kapoor, Sayash; Narayanan, Arvind
studies.title: Leakage and the Reproducibility Crisis in Machine-Learning-Based Science
studies.verification_basis: Crossref, Elsevier, and PMC full text verify metadata, DOI, taxonomy, and empirical reproducibility case study.
studies.evidence_anchor: Full text leakage taxonomy, 294-paper survey evidence, model information sheets, and corrected civil-war case study.
studies.assessment_note: Closest general precedent for a leakage-aware evidence contract and reproducibility audit. It does not join exact-fold explanations, SHAP stability, calibration, HR proxy-use boundaries, and manuscript-number hashes in one empirical HR package.

studies.authors: Guo, Chuan; Pleiss, Geoff; Sun, Yu; Weinberger, Kilian Q.
studies.title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
studies.venue: Proceedings of the 34th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 70, 1321-1330
studies.verification_basis: Official PMLR record provides title, authors, venue, volume, pages, year, abstract, full paper, supplement, and BibTeX.
studies.evidence_anchor: Official paper evaluating post-processing calibration methods including temperature scaling.
studies.assessment_note: Calibration foundation. It supports fitting post-hoc calibration on data separate from final evaluation and reporting metric-specific effects rather than treating accuracy as probability quality.

studies.authors: Vaicenavicius, Juozas; Widmann, David; Andersson, Carl; Lindsten, Fredrik; Roll, Jacob; Schön, Thomas B.
studies.title: Evaluating Model Calibration in Classification
studies.venue: Proceedings of the Twenty-Second International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics, PMLR 89, 3459-3467
studies.verification_basis: Official PMLR record provides title, authors, venue, volume, pages, year, abstract, full paper, supplement, and BibTeX.
studies.evidence_anchor: Official paper's probabilistic calibration framework and reliability visualizations.
studies.assessment_note: Calibration-evaluation foundation that motivates classwise and multidimensional reliability diagnostics and cautions against a single scalar calibration claim.

studies.authors: Mitchell, Margaret; Wu, Simone; Zaldivar, Andrew; Barnes, Parker; Vasserman, Lucy; Hutchinson, Ben; Spitzer, Elena; Raji, Inioluwa Deborah; Gebru, Timnit
studies.title: Model Cards for Model Reporting
studies.venue: Proceedings of the Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency, 220-229
studies.verification_basis: Crossref and ACM publisher metadata verify title, authors, venue, pages, year, and DOI.
studies.evidence_anchor: Publisher paper specifying transparent model reporting across intended uses, evaluation, and groups.
studies.assessment_note: Reporting precedent for intended-use, metric, and subgroup disclosure. Model cards are documentation rather than the hash-bound data/model/fold/manuscript lineage required here.

studies.authors: Pineau, Joelle; Vincent-Lamarre, Philippe; Sinha, Koustuv; Larivière, Vincent; Beygelzimer, Alina; d'Alché-Buc, Florence; Fox, Emily; Larochelle, Hugo
studies.title: Improving Reproducibility in Machine Learning Research (A Report from the NeurIPS 2019 Reproducibility Program)
studies.verification_basis: Official JMLR record and full paper verify title, authors, issue/article, pages, year, and reproducibility-program content.
studies.evidence_anchor: Full paper on code submission, reproducibility challenge, and checklist requirements for data, preprocessing, sample allocation, hyperparameters, runs, and uncertainty.
studies.assessment_note: Reproducibility-program precedent for transparent data/code/method reporting. It does not require immutable hashes joining every reported manuscript number to a particular model and fold identity.

excluded_candidates.candidate: Public INX Future Inc GitHub repositories and portfolio pages
excluded_candidates.reason: Useful discovery evidence for the dataset lineage, but code projects and resumes are not treated as peer-reviewed studies or bibliographic authorities.

excluded_candidates.candidate: A Simulation of the Impacts of Machine Learning to Combine Psychometric Employee Selection System Predictors on Performance Prediction
excluded_candidates.reason: Valid personnel-selection study, but less directly aligned than the retained exact-dataset, HR-XAI, and evidence-contract sources within the 25-work cap.

excluded_candidates.candidate: Employees' Perceptions of the Fairness of AI-Based Performance Prediction Features
excluded_candidates.reason: Relevant perception evidence, but it does not evaluate the model-audit mechanisms compared in the positioning table.

excluded_candidates.candidate: Application of Machine Learning in Predicting Performance and Optimizing the Recruitment Process
excluded_candidates.reason: Publisher abstract was located, but dataset identity and the requested audit fields could not be verified closely enough to displace a retained source.

excluded_candidates.candidate: AI-Driven Transparent Employee Performance Appraisal and Development Systems
excluded_candidates.reason: Search metadata suggested relevance, but primary full-method evidence was not accessible during this bounded audit.

excluded_candidates.candidate: Explainable Learning Analytics: Assessing the Stability of Student Success Prediction Models by Means of Explainable AI
excluded_candidates.reason: Strong SHAP-stability analogue, but student success is less close than retained SHAP robustness sources plus employee-domain studies.
